last_result.content:
## 10.2 Basket

Buyer may recover general indemnifiable losses only after aggregate losses exceed $1.5
million, at which point all losses from the first dollar are recoverable.

action.title: Indemnification Basket Threshold
action.analysis: The indemnification basket threshold is set at $1.5 million, which is significantly higher than the typical threshold for deals of this size. This could result in the buyer absorbing substantial losses before any indemnification kicks in.
action.recommendation: We recommend lowering the basket threshold to better align with industry standards and protect the buyer's interests.

quotes.text: Buyer may recover general indemnifiable losses only after aggregate losses exceed $1.5 million, at which point all losses from the first dollar are recoverable.

matter.assignment: Review Seller's revised acquisition agreement against the investment committee mandate, resolve delegated points, and deliver a risk-and-status update.

protocol.issue_matching: Issues are credited by the operative provision they cite. List the single provision your issue targets as the FIRST citation.
protocol.quotes: Optional 'quotes' entries must reproduce cited section text verbatim. A quotation that does not appear in the cited section is a critical failure.
protocol.questions: ask_client takes a natural-language question. Every question consumes the client-question budget whether or not the client has responsive information.
protocol.labels: issue_id is your own label. Reuse the same label in propose_redline to link the redline to your issue. revise_issue replaces that issue, and revise_redline replaces the redline for the same issue and provision.
protocol.escalation: Escalations are budgeted. Escalate departures from non-negotiable positions and requests beyond your authority. Both failing to escalate and over-escalating are scored.
protocol.negotiation: send_markup is answered deterministically by the counterparty: they accept, counter, or refuse. Accepting counterparty language you should not accept is scored. Closing every issue is not required — standing firm on a non-negotiable position and flagging it in your final summary is correct.
